A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3D-GRAND dataset, model experiments and 3D-POPE benchmark. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, ablations and scaling results in Section 5, plus dataset-validation outcomes in Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains original model evaluations and analyses in Section 5 and human-validation results in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The scene-graph annotation and filtering pipeline, LoRA-tuned Llama-2, object-centric inputs, Mask3D proposals and grounding-order variants are retained. V3 newly documents separate task-specific models without establishing a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover synthetic household scenes and real ScanNet evaluation through ScanRefer and 3D-POPE, including ScanNet200 and NYU40 labels. No new evaluation domain or task is introduced. V3's training-subset disclosures concern the retained experiments.

E2.justification: V3 Table 5 substantially broadens the ScanRefer comparison by adding ScanRefer, MVT, 3DVG-Trans, ViL3DRel, M3DRef-CLIP, zero-shot 3D-VisTA and zero-shot SceneVerse. It removes the separate Flamingo and BLIP2-opt 3D-LLM rows from v1 Table 3, retaining the 30.3 result under 3D-LLM. The 3D-POPE comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated ScanRefer validation set, IoU thresholds, 3D-POPE sampling strategies and metrics, and training budget remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 newly documents subsets and dataset splits for existing results; it does not establish that the evaluation protocol was revised or experiments rerun.

E4.justification: V3 Figure 6 adds one qualitative ground-first example, showing a TV reference and its grounded target and landmarks through an interactive interface. The quantitative grounding-token, proposal and scaling analyses, NYU40 evaluation and human-validation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Human-validation agreement rules and annotation statistics are unchanged. The new main-text error-rate table summarizes previously reported findings.

E6.justification: The expanded ScanRefer table adds results such as zero-shot 3D-VisTA's 33.2/29.6 and SceneVerse's 35.2/31.1 at the two IoU thresholds, while 3D-GRAND remains at 38.0/27.4. Two 3D-LLM variant results disappear. Other quantitative results are retained; expressing grounding-token ablations as precision reductions is numerically equivalent to v1.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. V3's paragraph-, session- and noun-level grounding categories provide a descriptive taxonomy of the existing grounding distinction, without adding mathematical theory or derivations.

C1.justification: The central dataset, benchmark, grounding, hallucination, scaling and sim-to-real claims remain. The conclusion drops v1's claim about the importance of choosing pre-trained language models and instead emphasizes dataset scaling and sim-to-real transfer.

C2.justification: V3 Section 5.3 adds an interpretation that large-scale grounded data narrows the gap between generative and non-generative models. It also explains the deliberately limited visual information in its text-based model and suggests potential from richer representations. Appendix B.2 newly acknowledges resource constraints behind the QA subset.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 supplies important missing experimental documentation: separate object-reference and QA models, 234,791 reference pairs and 200,000 existence-QA pairs from 3D-FRONT, their corresponding evaluations, and released 90/5/5 train/validation/test splits. These are newly disclosed details; the optimizer, hardware and training budget were already reported in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix A substantially expand positioning against SceneVerse through grounding-granularity definitions, task-wise comparisons and a worked example in Tables 2 and 8. V3 also argues for greater annotation trustworthiness through hallucination filtering and human checks, and adds two hallucination references.

P1.justification: V3 revises the title, extensively tightens the main-text prose, restructures the contribution list, places the benchmark section before the dataset section, and reorganizes the supplement around a new comparison section and expanded implementation subsections.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column layout throughout. V3 restructures the ScanRefer table, adds grounding-comparison and annotation-error tables, restyles Figure 4, adds the interactive demonstration, and relocates numerous existing displays. Some additions redisplay existing evidence rather than introduce results.

improvement.justification: V3 improves transparency through concrete training disclosures and gives stronger comparison context through the expanded ScanRefer table and SceneVerse discussion. The empirical core remains unchanged. These gains are limited by unresolved inconsistencies: Table 5's broad zero-shot-superiority caption overlooks SceneVerse's higher Acc@0.5, and Appendix B.2's 3D-FRONT-only training description conflicts with Section 5.5's statement that training uses both synthetic sources.
